Background

In the data folder, you will find data about shark incidents in California between 1950-2022. The data are from: State of California- Shark Incident Database.

Load the libraries

library("tidyverse")
library("janitor")

Load the data

Run the following code chunk to import the data. In this chunk, I am removing NA’s.

sharks <- 
  read_csv("data/SharkIncidents_1950_2022_220302.csv", 
           na=c("NA", "N/A", "Unknown", "NOT COUNTED", "", " ")) %>% 
  clean_names()

Questions

  1. Are there any “hotspots” for shark incidents in California? Show the top five counties with the most incidents.
names(sharks)
##  [1] "incident_num"     "month"            "day"              "year"            
##  [5] "time"             "county"           "location"         "mode"            
##  [9] "injury"           "depth"            "species"          "comment"         
## [13] "longitude"        "latitude"         "confirmed_source" "wfl_case_number"
sharks %>%
  count(county, sort = T) %>% 
  slice_head(n=5)
## # A tibble: 5 × 2
##   county            n
##   <chr>         <int>
## 1 San Diego        25
## 2 Humboldt         20
## 3 San Mateo        19
## 4 Santa Barbara    19
## 5 Marin            16
  1. Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents per county.
sharks %>%
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x=county, fill=county))+
  geom_bar()+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title="Shark Incidents Per County",  x="County", y="Incidents")

  1. Are there months of the year when incidents are more likely to occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by month. Which month has the highest number of incidents?
    October has the highest number of shark incidents.
sharks %>%
  mutate(across(c("month"), as.factor)) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x=month, fill=month))+
  geom_bar()+
  labs(title="Shark Incidents By Month",  x="Month", y="Incidents")

  1. Is there a time of day when most attacks occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by time of day. Which time of day has the highest number of incidents?
    1:30pm has the highest number of incidents.
sharks %>%
  na.omit() %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x=time, fill=time))+
  geom_bar()+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title="Shark Incidents By Time",  x="Time", y="Incidents")

  1. How do the number and types of injuries compare by county? Make a table that shows the number of injury types by county. Which county has the highest number incidents? (hint: your table should be in wide format) San Diego has the highest number of incidents
names(sharks)
##  [1] "incident_num"     "month"            "day"              "year"            
##  [5] "time"             "county"           "location"         "mode"            
##  [9] "injury"           "depth"            "species"          "comment"         
## [13] "longitude"        "latitude"         "confirmed_source" "wfl_case_number"
sharks_wide <- sharks %>% 
  count(county,injury) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = injury,values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>% 
  mutate(total = minor + none + major + `minor*` + `none*` + fatal + `major*`) %>% 
  arrange(desc(total))
sharks_wide
## # A tibble: 22 × 9
##    county          minor  none major `minor*` `none*` fatal `major*` total
##    <chr>           <int> <int> <int>    <int>   <int> <int>    <int> <int>
##  1 San Diego           8     9     4        1       1     2        0    25
##  2 Humboldt            2     9     7        1       1     0        0    20
##  3 San Mateo           4    12     1        1       0     1        0    19
##  4 Santa Barbara       6     9     2        0       0     2        0    19
##  5 Marin               4     3     9        0       0     0        0    16
##  6 Monterey            2     3     8        0       0     2        1    16
##  7 Santa Cruz          3     8     3        0       0     1        0    15
##  8 Sonoma              1     6     8        0       0     0        0    15
##  9 San Luis Obispo     1     7     3        0       0     3        0    14
## 10 Los Angeles         6     2     0        0       0     1        1    10
## # ℹ 12 more rows
  1. Use the table from #5 to make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by county.
sharks_wide %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x=county, y=total, fill = county))+
  geom_col()+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title="Shark Incidents Per County",  x="County", y="Incidents")

  1. In the data, mode refers to a type of activity. Which activity is associated with the highest number of incidents? Surfing/Boarding is associated with the highest number of incidents
sharks_activity_wide <- sharks %>% 
  count(mode) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = mode,values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
sharks_activity_wide
## # A tibble: 1 × 8
##   Freediving `Hookah Diving` `Kayaking / Canoeing` Paddleboarding `Scuba Diving`
##        <int>           <int>                 <int>          <int>          <int>
## 1         36              10                    30              7             20
## # ℹ 3 more variables: `Surfing / Boarding` <int>, Swimming <int>,
## #   `Walking in shallow` <int>
  1. Make a plot that compares the number of incidents by activity.
sharks %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x=mode, fill=mode))+
  geom_bar()+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title="Shark Incidents By Activity",  x="Activity", y="Count")

9. Which shark species is involved in the highest number of incidents?
Great White Sharks are involved in the highest number of incidents.

sharks_species_wide <- sharks %>% 
  count(species) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = species,values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
sharks_species_wide
## # A tibble: 1 × 12
##    Blue `Blue*` Hammerhead `Killer Whale` Leopard  Mako Salmon Sevengill
##   <int>   <int>      <int>          <int>   <int> <int>  <int>     <int>
## 1     2       1          3              2       2     1      2         1
## # ℹ 4 more variables: Thresher <int>, White <int>, blue <int>, `NA` <int>
  1. Are all incidents involving Great White’s fatal? Make a plot that shows the number and types of incidents for Great White’s only.
sharks%>% 
  filter(species=="White") %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x=injury, fill=injury))+
  geom_bar()+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title="Types and Numbers of Great White Shark Incidents",  x="Type", y="Number of Incidents")+
  theme(plot.title=element_text(size=rel(1.5), hjust=.5))
